data.current_summary: Look up a company by global identifier
data.current_description: Returns the base record, identical in every country, plus the blocks requested with include. France (FR), Belgium (BE), Switzerland (CH), Norway (NO), Finland (FI), Latvia (LV), Ireland (IE), Sweden (SE), Estonia (EE), Lithuania (LT), Australia (AU), Singapore (SG), Japan (JP) and the United Kingdom (GB) are available. Belgian enterprise numbers have 10 digits with a modulo-97 check (BE-0417497106); 0417.497.106, BE0417497106 and the old 9-digit form are accepted. Swiss identifiers are CH- and the 9 digits of the UID without the CHE prefix (CH-101374515 for CHE-101.374.515), whose last digit is a modulo-11 check (eCH-0097); CH-CHE-101.374.515 and CH-CHE-101.374.515 MWST are accepted. In Switzerland, activity and incorporated_on are null (not provided for Switzerland) and closed_on stays null for a closed entity. Norwegian identifiers are NO- and the 9 digits of the organisation number, whose last digit is a modulo-11 check (NO-923609016); 923 609 016 and NO923609016MVA are accepted after the prefix. Finnish identifiers are FI- and the 8 characters of the Business ID without the hyphen, with a modulo-11 check (FI-01120389 for 0112038-9); FI-0112038-9 is accepted. Latvian identifiers are LV- and the 11 digits of the registration number (LV-40003245752), which has no published check digit. In Latvia, activity is null; in Norway and Finland, closed_on stays null for an entity that left the register. Irish identifiers are IE- and the company number without leading zeros (IE-104547), which has no published check digit; the vat block is not available in Ireland. Swedish identifiers are SE- and the 10 digits of the organisation number, whose last digit is a Luhn check (SE-5560427220); 556042-7220, SE5560427220 and SE556042722001 are accepted. In Sweden, the activity code has no label and nace is null. Estonian identifiers are EE- and the 8 digits of the registry code, whose last digit is a check digit (EE-10137025); EE10137025 and the VAT number EE100210460 are accepted. In Estonia, nace is given for EMTAK 2008 codes only. Lithuanian identifiers are LT- and the 9 digits of the legal entity code, whose last digit is a check digit (LT-110053842); LT110053842 (the VAT number) is accepted. In Lithuania, activity is null and the address block is not available. Australian identifiers are AU- and the 11 digits of the ABN (AU-51824753556), with a modulo-89 check; 51 824 753 556 and ABN 51824753556 are accepted. In Australia, activity is null, there is no street address (state and postcode only) and a sole trader is served under its trading name. Singapore identifiers are SG- and the UEN (SG-196800306E for a company, SG-53012345A style for a business, SG-T05LL0003J style for another entity), whose last letter is a check letter; closed_on stays null. In Singapore, activity is the SSIC code and nace is null. Japanese identifiers are JP- and the 13 digits of the corporate number (JP-1180301018771), whose first digit is a check digit. In Japan, names and addresses are in Japanese, activity is null and incorporated_on is null.
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves company information by identifier across 14 countries (FR, BE, CH, GB, NO, FI, LV, IE, SE, EE, LT, AU, SG, JP). Returns the base V2Company record with optional data blocks specified via the include parameter. Identifier formats vary by country and support multiple formats (with or without country prefix, alternative separators). Country-specific data availability varies: some fields are null in certain countries (e.g., activity in Latvia, Lithuania, Australia; address in Lithuania; vat in Ireland). Use the include parameter to request additional data blocks beyond the base record.

data.current_summary: Search companies by name, or find a registry number in every country served
data.current_description:
Give either q or registry_id; q takes precedence when both are given.

With q (name search), every word of 2 characters or more must appear in the company name, the last word as a prefix of 3 letters or more ("dano" finds DANONE). Case, accents and punctuation are ignored. Results come in this order: exact names first (legal forms such as SA, SAS, SARL, LTD or PLC are ignored when comparing, so "danone" finds DANONE first), then active companies, then companies before sole traders, then relevance. Very common words are served without relevance ranking after 400 ms, so that results stay fast. Without country, every country with a name index is searched. Results are base records, as returned by GET /v2/companies/{id}; include is not applied. The whole search counts as one request. Units whose publication is restricted (diffusion status P) have no name and cannot be found by name.

With registry_id, for clients that only know the national number: lists the companies of every country served that carry this number, usually one; an empty list if none, sorted by identifier.

Name search requires all words of 2+ characters to appear in the company name, with the last word matching as a 3+ character prefix (case, accents, and punctuation ignored). Results are ordered by: exact name matches first, then active companies, then sole traders, then relevance. Registry identifier search returns all matching companies across served countries. Returns base V2Company records without optional blocks (include parameter not applied). Restricted-publication companies (diffusion status P) are not searchable by name. Each search counts as one request.

data.current_summary: Check a company identifier, a SIRET and a VAT number in one call
data.current_description: Give id, siret, vat, or any combination of them (at least one). Spaces, dots and hyphens are ignored in siret and vat. Each check is returned with its result; a check that depends on a failed one is omitted (a malformed SIRET is not looked up). valid is true only if every check returned is ok. company is the base record with its address (and its vat block when a VAT number was checked); it is returned even when the establishment or the company is closed, and is null when the identifiers do not point to the same company or the company is not found. French, Belgian, Swiss, Norwegian (NO, the organisation number and MVA), Finnish (FI), Latvian (LV), Swedish (SE) and Estonian (EE) VAT numbers have a register here. The VAT number of any other member state of the European Union (AT BE BG CY CZ DE DK EE EL ES FI FR HR HU IE IT LT LU LV MT NL PL PT RO SE SI SK, and XI for Northern Ireland; GR is read as EL) is checked too: its shape per country, then the official service, and the vat block of the response gives the status, the date and time of the check, the name and address when the company agreed to publish them and the consultation identifier when available. A member state that does not answer gives the status unverifiable (valid null, the check passes, the response is not cached, a retry runs in the background). A valid number is reused for 24 hours, an invalid one for 1 hour. Numbers of the European Union member states and of Northern Ireland (XI) are checked with the official European verification service, GB numbers with the official British one. A French EORI is FR followed by the SIREN (9 digits, the form to use) or, for former numbers, FR followed by the SIRET (14 digits); other lengths are refused. An unverifiable answer is sent with Cache-Control: no-store.
data.description_suggestion: Verifies an EORI (Economic Operator Registration and Identification) customs number against official services. EORI format: two-letter country code followed by up to 15 letters or digits (spaces, dots, hyphens ignored; EL mapped to GR). Supported countries: EU member states, Northern Ireland (XI), and GB (verified against respective official services). Switzerland (CH) and Norway (NO) return status not_applicable as EORI does not apply. French EORI must be FR + SIREN (9 digits, preferred) or FR + SIRET (14 digits for legacy numbers). Returns operator name and address only when the official service provides them and the operator consents to publication. Unverifiable responses (when official services don't answer) return valid=null and are not reported as invalid; these responses are sent with Cache-Control: no-store. Valid answers are cached 24 hours; calls to official services are rate-limited. Counts as one request.

data.current_summary: Look up a company by global identifier
data.current_description: Returns the base record, identical in every country, plus the blocks requested with include. France (FR), Belgium (BE), Switzerland (CH), Norway (NO), Finland (FI), Latvia (LV), Ireland (IE), Sweden (SE), Estonia (EE), Lithuania (LT), Australia (AU), Singapore (SG), Japan (JP) and the United Kingdom (GB) are available. Belgian enterprise numbers have 10 digits with a modulo-97 check (BE-0417497106); 0417.497.106, BE0417497106 and the old 9-digit form are accepted. Swiss identifiers are CH- and the 9 digits of the UID without the CHE prefix (CH-101374515 for CHE-101.374.515), whose last digit is a modulo-11 check (eCH-0097); CH-CHE-101.374.515 and CH-CHE-101.374.515 MWST are accepted. In Switzerland, activity and incorporated_on are null (not provided for Switzerland) and closed_on stays null for a closed entity. Norwegian identifiers are NO- and the 9 digits of the organisation number, whose last digit is a modulo-11 check (NO-923609016); 923 609 016 and NO923609016MVA are accepted after the prefix. Finnish identifiers are FI- and the 8 characters of the Business ID without the hyphen, with a modulo-11 check (FI-01120389 for 0112038-9); FI-0112038-9 is accepted. Latvian identifiers are LV- and the 11 digits of the registration number (LV-40003245752), which has no published check digit. In Latvia, activity is null; in Norway and Finland, closed_on stays null for an entity that left the register. Irish identifiers are IE- and the company number without leading zeros (IE-104547), which has no published check digit; the vat block is not available in Ireland. Swedish identifiers are SE- and the 10 digits of the organisation number, whose last digit is a Luhn check (SE-5560427220); 556042-7220, SE5560427220 and SE556042722001 are accepted. In Sweden, the activity code has no label and nace is null. Estonian identifiers are EE- and the 8 digits of the registry code, whose last digit is a check digit (EE-10137025); EE10137025 and the VAT number EE100210460 are accepted. In Estonia, nace is given for EMTAK 2008 codes only. Lithuanian identifiers are LT- and the 9 digits of the legal entity code, whose last digit is a check digit (LT-110053842); LT110053842 (the VAT number) is accepted. In Lithuania, activity is null and the address block is not available. Australian identifiers are AU- and the 11 digits of the ABN (AU-51824753556), with a modulo-89 check; 51 824 753 556 and ABN 51824753556 are accepted. In Australia, activity is null, there is no street address (state and postcode only) and a sole trader is served under its trading name. Singapore identifiers are SG- and the UEN (SG-196800306E for a company, SG-53012345A style for a business, SG-T05LL0003J style for another entity), whose last letter is a check letter; closed_on stays null. In Singapore, activity is the SSIC code and nace is null. Japanese identifiers are JP- and the 13 digits of the corporate number (JP-1180301018771), whose first digit is a check digit. In Japan, names and addresses are in Japanese, activity is null and incorporated_on is null.

data.current_summary: Search companies by name, or find a registry number in every country served
data.current_description:
Give either q or registry_id; q takes precedence when both are given.

With q (name search), every word of 2 characters or more must appear in the company name, the last word as a prefix of 3 letters or more ("dano" finds DANONE). Case, accents and punctuation are ignored. Results come in this order: exact names first (legal forms such as SA, SAS, SARL, LTD or PLC are ignored when comparing, so "danone" finds DANONE first), then active companies, then companies before sole traders, then relevance. Very common words are served without relevance ranking after 400 ms, so that results stay fast. Without country, every country with a name index is searched. Results are base records, as returned by GET /v2/companies/{id}; include is not applied. The whole search counts as one request. Units whose publication is restricted (diffusion status P) have no name and cannot be found by name.

With registry_id, for clients that only know the national number: lists the companies of every country served that carry this number, usually one; an empty list if none, sorted by identifier.

data.current_summary: Check a company identifier, a SIRET and a VAT number in one call
data.current_description: Give id, siret, vat, or any combination of them (at least one). Spaces, dots and hyphens are ignored in siret and vat. Each check is returned with its result; a check that depends on a failed one is omitted (a malformed SIRET is not looked up). valid is true only if every check returned is ok. company is the base record with its address (and its vat block when a VAT number was checked); it is returned even when the establishment or the company is closed, and is null when the identifiers do not point to the same company or the company is not found. French, Belgian, Swiss, Norwegian (NO, the organisation number and MVA), Finnish (FI), Latvian (LV), Swedish (SE) and Estonian (EE) VAT numbers have a register here. The VAT number of any other member state of the European Union (AT BE BG CY CZ DE DK EE EL ES FI FR HR HU IE IT LT LU LV MT NL PL PT RO SE SI SK, and XI for Northern Ireland; GR is read as EL) is checked too: its shape per country, then the official service, and the vat block of the response gives the status, the date and time of the check, the name and address when the company agreed to publish them and the consultation identifier when available. A member state that does not answer gives the status unverifiable (valid null, the check passes, the response is not cached, a retry runs in the background). A valid number is reused for 24 hours, an invalid one for 1 hour. A country that is neither in the European Union nor served here gives vat_country_supported=false. siret applies to France only. eori adds the check of an EORI number (see GET /eori/{number}): its shape, then whether the official service knows it; a service that does not answer leaves the check passing with the value unverifiable, as the number is not proven wrong. A French EORI must be FR followed by the SIREN (9 digits) or by the SIRET of an establishment (14 digits), and that SIREN must be the one of the other identifiers. requester_vat (or the requester VAT number saved in the account settings) makes the check of a European VAT number in the name of the requester and returns the consultation identifier as proof of control; answers are cached per number and requester. Use cases: client and supplier onboarding forms, invoices (supplier SIRET and VAT), simple company identity checks. Counts as one request. Responses are sent with Cache-Control: private, max-age=60.

EORI validation includes format verification and official service confirmation. French EORI must be FR + SIREN (9 digits) or FR + SIRET (14 digits). Use for client/supplier onboarding, invoice verification, and company identity checks. Counts as one request. Responses cached with Cache-Control: private, max-age=60.

data.current_description: Checks an EORI number, the customs identifier of an economic operator: a two-letter country code followed by up to 15 letters or digits (spaces, dots and hyphens are ignored; EL is read as GR). Numbers of the European Union member states and of Northern Ireland (XI) are checked with the official European verification service, GB numbers with the official British one. Switzerland (CH) and Norway (NO) get status not_applicable: the European EORI does not apply there, and this is not an error. name and address are returned only when the official service gives them, that is when the operator agreed to their publication. An official service that cannot answer gives status unverifiable and valid null: it is never reported as invalid. Answers are reused for 24 hours per number, and calls toward the official services are paced. A French EORI is FR followed by the SIREN (9 digits, the form to use) or, for former numbers, FR followed by the SIRET (14 digits); other lengths are refused. GET /companies/{id}?include=eori tests FR + SIREN first, then FR + SIRET of the head office, and calls the number probable. Counts as one request. An unverifiable answer is sent with Cache-Control: no-store.
data.description_suggestion: Verifies an EORI (Economic Operator Registration and Identification) customs number against official services. EORI format: two-letter country code followed by up to 15 letters or digits (spaces, dots, hyphens ignored; EL mapped to GR). Supported countries: EU member states, Northern Ireland (XI), and GB (verified against respective official services). Switzerland (CH) and Norway (NO) return status not_applicable as EORI does not apply. French EORI must be FR + SIREN (9 digits, preferred) or FR + SIRET (14 digits for legacy numbers). Returns operator name and address only when the official service provides them and the operator consents to publication. Unverifiable responses (when official services don't answer) return valid=null and are not reported as invalid; these responses are sent with Cache-Control: no-store. Valid answers are cached 24 hours; calls to official services are rate-limited. Counts as one request.
